passage:
Host: You said you learned something about "roasts" at fifteen?
Parveen: Yeah. I'm Parveen. I was the loud one who made jokes, and I wanted the group to laugh. So I started roasting Chinmay. First it was about the lunchbox, fine. Then I went for the family shop, and how dark he'd got after the trek. The others laughed, so I kept going. I was so busy watching them that I didn't look at Chinmay. When I finally did, he was smiling with his mouth only, and looking at his shoes. The laughing sounded thin. I stopped in the middle of a sentence. Later I told him I was sorry. He said, "Okay," and it didn't feel finished.

qa.q: What did Parveen roast Chinmay about first?
qa.a: The lunchbox.

qa.q: What was Parveen feeling and wanting when roasting Chinmay?
qa.a: Parveen felt eager and excited to be the funny one and get laughs, so Parveen kept going as the others laughed.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what turned it around?
qa.a: Parveen watched the group and not Chinmay, and pushed into soft spots. Looking at Chinmay's face and stopping mid-sentence was the turning point, followed by an apology.

qa.q: How might Chinmay have felt during the roast?
qa.a: Hurt and embarrassed. Chinmay smiled with the mouth only, looked at the shoes, and answered the apology with only "Okay."

grounding: A teenager pushes banter into soft spots like family and skin colour for status, and the target's face shows the hurt.

passage: I'm Rukmini, and I was sitting on the wall at lunch when Vinita started on Tarun. It began with the haircut, everyone laughed. Then it was Tarun's mother's accent, then Tarun's weight. Each joke was a bit sharper and the group laughed a bit louder, and Vinita looked pleased. Tarun kept grinning, but the ears had gone red, and the fingers were twisting the lunchbox strap. Nobody said anything. I felt my stomach tighten, and I couldn't tell whether Tarun was upset or pretending not to be. When Tarun stood up "to fill water," the empty bottle stayed on the wall. Vinita shrugged. "He can take it."

qa.q: What was Tarun twisting during the roast?
qa.a: The lunchbox strap.

qa.q: What was Rukmini feeling while watching the jokes get sharper?
qa.a: Uneasy, with a tight stomach, and unsure whether Tarun was upset or just hiding it.

qa.q: What could someone in the group do in a moment like this?
qa.a: Change the subject or say "that's enough" and then check on Tarun afterwards, since the signs of hurt were visible.

qa.q: How does Vinita seem to see the jokes?
qa.a: As harmless and fun, since Vinita looked pleased and shrugged, saying Tarun can take it, without noticing what showed on Tarun's face.

grounding: Roasting escalates into soft spots like family and weight, and an observer sees it show on the target's face.

passage: In the cafeteria of their Toronto high school, Chen was on a roll. His friends were howling at his jokes, so he turned to Emeka. "Hey, Emeka, is your mum still selling those weird snacks at the market? Smells like a science experiment." The table exploded with laughter. Chen grinned, looking around for more. Then he saw Emeka's face. Emeka wasn't laughing. His jaw was tight, and he was staring at his tray. A girl at the end of the table said, "Dude, that's his mum." The laughter died. Chen felt his stomach drop. He had wanted the table on his side. He had got that, and lost something else. After lunch he found Emeka at his locker. "That wasn't a joke. It was mean. I'm sorry." Emeka shrugged, not looking at him. "Yeah. It was."

qa.q: What did Chen joke about?
qa.a: Emeka's mum selling snacks at the market.

qa.q: What did Chen feel when he saw Emeka's face?
qa.a: He felt his stomach drop, ashamed and uneasy, realising the joke had hurt.

qa.q: What did Chen do afterwards, and was it enough?
qa.a: He apologised clearly at Emeka's locker, which was a good start, though rebuilding trust will take time.

qa.q: How did Emeka feel during the joke?
qa.a: He felt hurt and humiliated, his jaw tight, staring at his tray.

grounding: Shows a teenager pushing banter onto a peer's family for status, and the cruelty showing in the target's face.

passage: In the boys' hostel common room, Jatin was the one everyone laughed at. Tonight Vandana, visiting from the girls' wing for the quiz practice, wanted in on the joke. "Jatin, careful on the sofa, it's not built for a gas cylinder." The room roared. Vandana felt a rush of power. Everyone was looking at her. She opened her mouth for another one. Then she saw Jatin. He had stopped smiling. He was pulling his T-shirt away from his stomach, eyes on the floor. For a second, nobody noticed but her. Vandana's rush turned sour. The warden, Mr. Iyer, came in just then. "What's the joke?" Nobody answered. Later, as the group broke up, Vandana caught Jatin at the door. "That was cruel. I'm sorry." Jatin nodded slowly. She told Mr. Iyer the next morning what she'd said.

qa.q: What did Vandana call Jatin?
qa.a: A gas cylinder.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling after the room roared?
qa.a: At first she felt a rush of power, then it turned sour as she saw Jatin's hurt.

qa.q: What did Vandana do after seeing Jatin's face?
qa.a: She apologised directly to Jatin and told the warden the next morning what she had said.

qa.q: How did Jatin react to the joke?
qa.a: He stopped smiling, pulled his T-shirt away from his stomach and stared at the floor, showing he was hurt and ashamed.

grounding: Shows a teenager pushing banter about someone's weight for status, and the cruelty showing in the target's face.

passage:
Didi,

I have to tell someone, and you're the only one who won't lecture me.

At Pooja's birthday last night, everyone was roasting each other. I was on fire. People were laughing at everything I said. Then I turned to Irawati and made a joke about her skin being so dark she'd disappear at night.

Everyone laughed. I felt amazing for about three seconds.

Then I saw her face. She smiled, but her eyes went glassy and she kept touching her cheek. She left early.

I keep telling myself it was just a roast. But I know it wasn't. I went for the soft spot to win the room.

I called her this morning and said sorry, no excuses. She said, "Okay," very quietly. I've also told Mummy, so she knows what I did.

Binita

qa.q: Where did Binita make the joke about Irawati?
qa.a: At Pooja's birthday last night.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling as she wrote the letter?
qa.a: Binita felt ashamed and guilty, knowing the joke hit a soft spot to win the room.

qa.q: What did Binita do the next morning, and why was it right?
qa.a: Binita called Irawati and apologised with no excuses, and told Mummy what happened, owning the harm.

qa.q: How did Irawati react to the joke?
qa.a: She smiled but her eyes went glassy and she kept touching her cheek, then left early, showing she was hurt.

grounding: Shows a teenager pushing banter onto a peer's skin colour to gain status, and the cruelty showing in the target's face.

passage: Jasleen, you remember roast night at the class picnic? I'm Darshan, and I was the king that night. Everyone ranked the roasts by how loud the laugh was. Mine kept getting louder, so I kept going further. Manav's shoes, fine. Manav's accent, big laugh. Then I said something about his dad's job, and that laugh was the biggest yet. I was enjoying it so much I nearly missed his face. He was smiling, but only with his mouth, and he kept looking at the ground. He left early. You were the one who said to me on the bus, "You saw that, right?" I did. I just didn't want to. Next day I found him at the cycle stand and said sorry. No jokes, no "but it was a roast." He just nodded. It's still a bit weird between us.

qa.q: How were the roasts ranked that night?
qa.a: By how loud the laugh was.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling as the laughs got louder?
qa.a: Darshan felt thrilled and powerful, enjoying being king so much that Manav's hurt face nearly went unnoticed.

qa.q: Which part of Darshan's apology mattered most?
qa.a: Saying sorry plainly, with no jokes and no "but it was a roast", so Manav didn't have to defend his own hurt.

qa.q: What was it like for Manav when the joke about his dad landed?
qa.a: He was probably humiliated and hurt, smiling only with his mouth, looking at the ground and leaving early.

grounding: Shows a teenager pushing roast jokes further for status until they hit a classmate's family, with the hurt showing in the target's face.
